description: Nudging moves route segments apart, so that connectors which share a channel (the free space between obstacles) no longer lie on top of each other. One pass moves the vertical segments and a second pass the horizontal ones; segments that end at a port stay fixed. *Separation constraints* of the form `x_v − x_u ≥ gap` keep the order of neighbouring segments, so routes keep their shape and get no new crossings. `connector-routing` solves them exactly, with no linear program: it finds the largest common gap and puts each segment midway in its free range. Full nudging (`full`) also lets boxes move and grow to make room.

papers.authors: Michael Wybrow, Kim Marriott, Peter J. Stuckey
papers.title: Orthogonal Connector Routing
A Simple Pipeline for Orthogonal Graph Drawing
papers.venue: Graph Drawing and Network Visualization (GD 2023), LNCS
